name: NVIDIA AI GPU
summary: From a design file to a rack of compute in a data center: an AI GPU passes through design, wafer fabrication, memory stacking, advanced packaging and system integration.

relatedIndustry.label: Racks are linked by optical modules: open the AI optical module supply chain

disclaimer: Illustrative flow for understanding supply-chain structure. It is not a bill of materials for any specific model, representative companies are not confirmed NVIDIA suppliers, and nothing here is investment advice.

sources.title: NVIDIA Docs — The NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Superchip (overview)

steps.title: Chip design
steps.tagline: NVIDIA only draws the blueprint; it owns no fabs. One GPU is built from two dies.
steps.process: Lay out the circuits, simulate and verify, then tape out
steps.bottleneck: Design and verification take years and are tied to one specific process, so switching foundries is very costly.
steps.evidence: NVIDIA states that Blackwell GPUs pack 208 billion transistors and use two reticle-limited dies joined by a 10 TB/s chip-to-chip link. The EDA vendors are generic industry examples.

steps.title: Silicon wafer
steps.tagline: Sand is purified into a single-crystal ingot, then sliced into mirror-flat 300mm discs.
steps.process: Melt → pull a crystal ingot → slice → grind and polish
steps.bottleneck: Leading-edge nodes need near-defect-free wafers; there are few suppliers and qualification is slow.
steps.evidence: Generic semiconductor process and representative suppliers. Their supply relationship to any specific GPU is not verified here.

steps.title: Lithography
steps.tagline: Extreme-ultraviolet light projects the circuit pattern onto the wafer, one die at a time.
steps.process: EUV light passes the mask, is reduced by the optics, and exposes die after die
steps.bottleneck: Only ASML can build EUV scanners. It is the most concentrated equipment step in the whole chain.
steps.evidence: NVIDIA confirms Blackwell is manufactured on a custom TSMC 4NP process. ASML is the only supplier of EUV lithography systems. Resist vendors are industry examples.

steps.title: Etch and deposition
steps.tagline: Deposit, pattern, etch — repeated hundreds of times to build transistors and wiring layer by layer.
steps.process: Deposit films, etch away the excess, clean, inspect, repeat
steps.output: Finished wafer full of GPU dies
steps.bottleneck: A leading-edge wafer spends months in the fab, so capacity cannot be added quickly, and yield decides real output.
steps.evidence: Generic process flow and representative equipment makers, not a confirmed supplier list for any specific GPU.

steps.title: Wafer test and dicing
steps.tagline: Every die is probed, bad ones are marked, and the wafer is cut apart. Only good dies move on.
steps.process: Probe each die → mark failures → dice
steps.bottleneck: GPU dies are huge, so a wafer yields few of them and a single defect scraps a whole die.
steps.evidence: Generic flow and representative companies. The actual test outsourcing split is not verified.

steps.title: High-bandwidth memory
steps.tagline: A second production line running in parallel: DRAM dies stacked vertically and wired through with vias.
steps.process: Drill vias (TSV) → thin → stack and bond layer by layer → test
steps.bottleneck: Only three companies mass-produce HBM. Stacking yield and customer qualification gate supply: no HBM, no GPU shipments.
steps.evidence: That these three are the main HBM makers is industry consensus. Their share in any given GPU model is not verified here.

steps.title: CoWoS advanced packaging
steps.tagline: The two lines meet here: GPU dies and HBM sit side by side on an interposer, which is mounted on a substrate.
steps.input: GPU dies, HBM, interposer, ABF substrate
steps.bottleneck: The best-known choke point for AI GPU shipments in recent years: packaging capacity, interposers and large substrates must all scale together.
steps.evidence: CoWoS is TSMC's 2.5D packaging technology (official material). Blackwell's use of CoWoS-L and the substrate vendors come from public industry reporting and are not individually verified; current capacity tightness needs separate checking.

steps.title: Module and server assembly
steps.tagline: Packaged GPUs go onto a board with power delivery and liquid cold plates, then the system is tested.
steps.input: GPU packages, CPU, PCB, power, cold plates
steps.process: Mount → fit cold plates and tubing → flash firmware → burn-in test
steps.bottleneck: Each chip draws so much power that power delivery and cooling have become the new engineering limit; air cooling is no longer enough.
steps.evidence: NVIDIA states that a GB200 superchip combines two Blackwell GPUs with one Grace CPU and that NVL72 is liquid-cooled. The manufacturers are representative companies from public reporting; the per-model split is not verified.

steps.title: Rack and data center
steps.tagline: 72 GPUs fill one liquid-cooled rack, and racks are linked by fast networking and optical modules into an AI factory.
steps.input: Compute trays, switches, power, cooling, optics
steps.process: Integrate the rack → power-on acceptance → connect to the data-center network
steps.output: Compute ready for training and inference
steps.bottleneck: A finished chip is not yet online compute: power, liquid-cooling infrastructure and optical interconnect set the pace of deployment.
steps.evidence: NVIDIA states that GB200 NVL72 is a liquid-cooled rack-scale system with 72 Blackwell GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs in a single 72-GPU NVLink domain.
